title: Popular Differences and the Croot--Lev Half-Threshold Problem
summary: Let $A$ be a finite non-empty subset of an abelian group $G$, and let $r_A(d)=|\{(a,a')\in A^2:a-a'=d\}|$. Croot and Lev asked whether the pointwise half-threshold condition $r_A(d)\ge |A|/2$ for every $d\in A-A$ forces $A-A$ to be either a subgroup or a union of three cosets. We resolve this open problem in its sharp general form by identifying the essential obstruction: the statement is false in arbitrary abelian groups, but becomes true after excluding non-zero two-torsion.
